functionality.rationale: The runtime must turn completed TLS and pairing primitives into real connections without inventing identity, session, or transcript state.

security.rationale: ALPN confusion, unpinned established channels, malformed certificates, or discovery-derived identity would break the accepted pairing security profile.

performance.rationale: Handshake, frame assembly, timers, and connection limits must remain bounded under slow or hostile peers.

compatibility.rationale: Both registered ALPN modes and existing TLS, session, and identity contracts must remain wire and source compatible.

concurrency.rationale: Socket, SSL, timer, executor, session callback, and engine shutdown lifetimes race across asynchronous completion.

platform.rationale: Asio socket and OpenSSL lifecycle behavior must hold across macOS, Windows, and Linux production builds.

persistence.rationale: Inbound exact-pin resolution and trust commit consume protected identity records and must fail closed on unavailable or corrupt storage.

adr.rationale: The task implements the accepted security profile and ALPN demultiplexing decision without changing it.

architecture.rationale: The existing engine-owned worker runtime and TLS/session dependency direction remain unchanged.

roadmap.rationale: XT-032 closes pairing only after the complete vertical-slice evidence passes.
